ei.subject: ReadingPower유형편완성

fullPassage: Some researchers assumed that early human beings ate mainly the muscle flesh of animals, as we do today. By "meat," they meant the muscle of the animal. Yet focusing on the muscle appears to be a relatively recent phenomenon. In every history on the subject, the evidence suggests that early human populations preferred the fat and organ meat of the animal over its muscle meat. Vilhjalmur Stefansson, an arctic explorer, found that the Inuit were careful to save fatty meat and organs for human consumption while giving muscle meat to the dogs. In this way, humans ate as other large, meat-eating mammals eat. Lions and tigers, for instance, first eat the blood, hearts, livers, and brains of the animals they kill, often leaving the muscle meat for eagles. These organs tend to be much higher in fat.

questions.passage: Some researchers (A)[assumed / denied] that early human beings ate mainly the muscle flesh of animals, as we do today. By "meat," they meant the muscle of the animal. Yet focusing on the muscle appears to be a relatively recent phenomenon. In every history on the subject, the evidence suggests that early human populations (B)[preferred / rejected] the fat and organ meat of the animal over its muscle meat. Vilhjalmur Stefansson, an arctic explorer, found that the Inuit were careful to save fatty meat and organs for human consumption while giving muscle meat to the dogs. In this way, humans ate as other large, meat-eating mammals eat. Lions and tigers, for instance, first eat the blood, hearts, livers, and brains of the animals they kill, often leaving the muscle meat for eagles. These organs tend to be much (C)[lower / higher] in fat.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) assumed(추정했다), (B) preferred(선호했다), (C) higher(더 높은) — 원문 일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① denied — preferred — higher: denied는 assumed의 반의어
❌ ② assumed — rejected — higher: rejected는 preferred의 반의어
❌ ③ assumed — preferred — lower: lower는 higher의 반의어
✅ ④ assumed — preferred — higher: 원문 그대로

questions.passage: Some researchers assumed that early human beings ate mainly the muscle flesh of animals, as we do today. By "meat," they meant the muscle of the animal. In this way, humans ate as other large, meat-eating mammals eat. Lions and tigers, for instance, first eat the blood, hearts, livers, and brains of the animals they kill, often (C)[leaving / collecting] the muscle meat for eagles. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) focusing(집중하는 것), (B) save(보관하다), (C) leaving(남기다) — 원문 일치

✅ ① focusing — save — leaving: 원문 그대로
❌ ② focusing — waste — leaving: waste는 save의 반의어
❌ ③ ignoring — save — leaving: ignoring은 focusing의 반의어
❌ ④ focusing — save — collecting: collecting은 leaving의 반의어

det.korean: (A) evidence(증거), (B) careful(주의 깊은), (C) tend(~하는 경향이 있다) — 원문 일치

❌ ③ evidence — careful — fail: fail은 tend의 맥락적 반의어
✅ ④ evidence — careful — tend: 원문 그대로

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 organ의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) organ = 장기(신체 기관), (B) organ = 오르간(악기)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 장기 — (B) 오르간: 수술 후 기능 → 신체 장기, 성당에서 소리 → 악기
❌ ② (A) 장기 — (B) 장기: (B)는 성당에서 울리는 소리 → 악기
❌ ③ (A) 오르간 — (B) 장기: 순서 반대
❌ ④ (A) 오르간 — (B) 오르간: (A)는 수술/환자 맥락 → 장기

questions.passage: Some researchers assumed that early human beings ate mainly the muscle flesh of animals, as we do today. By "meat," they meant the muscle of the animal. Yet focusing on the muscle appears to be a relatively recent phenomenon. In every history on the subject, the evidence suggests that early human populations preferred __________ of the animal over its muscle meat. Vilhjalmur Stefansson, an arctic explorer, found that the Inuit were careful to save fatty meat and organs for human consumption while giving muscle meat to the dogs. In this way, humans ate as other large, meat-eating mammals eat. Lions and tigers, for instance, first eat the blood, hearts, livers, and brains of the animals they kill, often leaving the muscle meat for eagles. These organs tend to be much higher in fat.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
